Country-code domains and every suffix, including .com, .org, and .dev. The app reads the RDAP service list published by IANA, then queries the registry for that suffix. Suffixes without RDAP use the WHOIS server published by IANA. The query leaves your device directly. It does not pass through the author\'s server or a third-party lookup API.
The registry returned the original text, but it contains almost no standard fields. Open the raw record to read the full text.

1. Open source and free. Use only the official source
ToolBox is free and open source. The source is published only at %1$s under the %2$s. Anyone may download, use, modify, and distribute it at no charge.
The author has never published a paid edition in any app store or third-party channel. There is no membership, in-app purchase, unlock code, or payment to remove ads.

If you paid for ToolBox somewhere, or someone charged you for a \"premium\", \"pro\", or \"lifetime\" edition, request a refund and report that seller. You bought a resale of free open-source software. A price means the source is not genuine.
This app contains two separate tools. It is not a cloud service, it has no accounts, and it does not ask you to register or sign in.

SSH / SFTP: connect to a remote host you control (Linux, macOS, Windows OpenSSH, and similar). Browse and manage files, view and edit text, compress and extract, calculate MD5 and SHA-256, and use an interactive shell.

Domain lookup: read the public registration record for country-code domains and generic domains such as .com, .org, and .dev. The app reads the RDAP service list published by IANA and queries the registry for that suffix. Suffixes without RDAP use the WHOIS server published by IANA.
Every connection is made directly between your device and the target server. There is no relay, and the developer cannot see what you send.
Domain lookups go from your device straight to IANA and to the registry or registrar for that suffix. The app does not send the query to the author and does not use a third-party lookup API.

The app does not collect or upload host addresses, ports, usernames, passwords, private keys, or remote file contents. The package contains no analytics SDK, advertising SDK, or crash-reporting SDK, and it does not ask for location, contacts, or SMS.

To avoid typing the same host twice, host settings and passwords are stored in this app\'s private storage (SharedPreferences in the Android private directory, with fields Base64-encoded, not encrypted). A rooted or compromised device may be able to read them. In a high-sensitivity environment, use key authentication and keep the device secure.
Uninstalling the app deletes that local data. You can also delete a saved host inside the app at any time.
Connecting to a remote host, transferring files, and running commands are network activity. Your carrier and the target server may log that traffic. This app does not control those logs.
Connect only to servers you own or that the owner has clearly authorized you to use.
Do not use this app for unauthorized access, scanning, intrusion, interference with someone else\'s system, or any illegal purpose.
Follow the laws where you are, the laws where the server is, and the rules set by the server owner.
You are responsible for commands you run in the terminal and for files you upload or download.

Remote file actions can delete, overwrite, move, or change permissions in ways that cannot be undone. Confirm each delete, overwrite, extract, rename, and permission change, and back up important data first.
Terminal commands run on the remote server. This app only sends them and shows the result. It does not guarantee that the result matches what you expected.
Domain data comes from the registry or registrar. Privacy policy may hide fields, and the data may not be live. This app shows only what the official interface returns.
